violations.rule_name: Invalid or Missing Consent Before Processing
violations.reason: Consent not in a valid active state at time of processing; Processing purpose does not match the purpose for which consent was obtained; Consent was bundled with T&Cs â€” void under Section 6(2)

explanation.why_detected: Data processing was detected without a valid active consent record. The transaction occurred after consent had expired, been revoked, or under bundled consent terms.
explanation.evidence: Data processing was detected without a valid active consent record. The transaction occurred after consent had expired, been revoked, or under bundled consent terms.
explanation.risk_reason: DPDP Act Section 6(1) requires a Data Fiduciary to process personal data only for purposes for which the Data Principal has given free, specific, informed, and unambiguous consent. Processing under invalid or expired consent violates this mandate.
mitigation: Obtain fresh explicit consent from affected data principals before resuming processing
Implement a consent management system that blocks processing when consent_status is not active
Conduct an audit of all transaction_events joined to expired consent records and pause affected workflows

violations.reason: Processing purpose directly contradicts the consented purpose; No notice was provided specifying the processing purpose before consent

explanation.why_detected: Personal data was processed for a purpose different from the one stated in the consent record, even where a technically active consent exists.
explanation.evidence: Personal data was processed for a purpose different from the one stated in the consent record, even where a technically active consent exists.
explanation.risk_reason: DPDP Act Section 4(1)(b) mandates that personal data be processed only for the specific lawful purpose for which it was collected. Processing for a different purpose — even under active consent — constitutes an unlawful act.
mitigation: Update transaction processing workflows to enforce purpose matching against consent records at runtime
Review and correct all consent records where consented_purpose differs from current processing activity
Implement purpose limitation controls in your data processing pipeline

explanation.why_detected: Personal data is being retained beyond its approved retention period, or retained after its processing purpose has been completed.
explanation.evidence: Personal data is being retained beyond its approved retention period, or retained after its processing purpose has been completed.
explanation.risk_reason: DPDP Act Section 8(7) requires a Data Fiduciary to delete personal data as soon as it is reasonable to assume that the purpose for which it was collected is no longer being served.
mitigation: Implement automated data deletion triggers based on retention_expiry_date and purpose_completed flags
Review the data_lifecycle table and immediately schedule deletion for all records where expiry has passed
Update your data inventory policy to include mandatory retention period review every 90 days

explanation.why_detected: Consent was collected without providing the required notice to the Data Principal, or through a channel that implies implicit or pre-ticked consent.
explanation.evidence: Consent was collected without providing the required notice to the Data Principal, or through a channel that implies implicit or pre-ticked consent.
explanation.risk_reason: DPDP Act Section 5 requires that before seeking consent, the Data Fiduciary must give a clear notice describing the personal data to be processed and the purpose. Consent without notice is invalid.
mitigation: Update all consent collection flows to display a layered notice before the consent request
Review and re-collect consent from all data principals where notice_provided is false
Implement a consent audit trail that captures notice delivery confirmation alongside consent capture

explanation.why_detected: Processing was identified for a minor without a verified guardian consent record.
explanation.evidence: Processing was identified for a minor without a verified guardian consent record.
explanation.risk_reason: DPDP Act Section 9 prohibits processing personal data of children without verifiable consent from their parent or guardian. This is a CRITICAL severity obligation with a maximum penalty of ₹200 crore.
mitigation: Implement age verification at account creation and flag all minor accounts immediately
Obtain and record guardian consent for all existing minor accounts before resuming data processing
Restrict all data processing on minor accounts until guardian consent is confirmed and recorded

explanation.evidence: Personal data is being processed or stored without encryption, leaving it exposed to unauthorized access or breach.
explanation.risk_reason: DPDP Act Section 8(5) requires Data Fiduciaries to implement reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches. Absence of encryption is a direct failure of this obligation.
mitigation: Immediately enable AES-256 encryption for all databases and storage systems containing PII
Audit all systems in system_inventory for encryption status and prioritize unencrypted systems

violations.reason: SLA deadline for fulfilling the erasure request has been exceeded; Data lifecycle record shows data has not been deleted despite request; No legal hold exists to justify withholding deletion

explanation.why_detected: An erasure request submitted by a Data Principal has not been fulfilled within the SLA period or remains in pending status.
explanation.evidence: An erasure request submitted by a Data Principal has not been fulfilled within the SLA period or remains in pending status.
explanation.risk_reason: DPDP Act Section 12(a) grants Data Principals the right to erasure of their personal data. Failure to honor this right within the prescribed SLA is a direct statutory violation.
mitigation: Implement an automated DSAR workflow with SLA countdown tracking and escalation alerts
Assign a responsible team to process all pending erasure requests within 24 hours
Conduct a review of all dsar_requests where sla_breached is true and provide a remediation timeline to the Board

explanation.evidence: Personal data is being retained even though the processing purpose has been completed and no deletion has been initiated.
explanation.risk_reason: DPDP Act Section 8(7)(a) requires that personal data not be retained beyond the period necessary for the purpose for which it was processed.
mitigation: Deploy automated retention management that triggers deletion when purpose_completed = true
Run an immediate purge job on all data_lifecycle records where purpose_completed is true and status is not deleted or pending_deletion
Update your data lifecycle policy to include a mandatory deletion SLA after purpose completion
